The test image shows a tomato plant that has collapsed/wilted severely — the whole plant is drooping/lying down with wilted, somewhat green leaves. No visible fungal growth or white mycelium. This looks like a vascular wilt disease. Key candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Verticillium_Wilt, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus.

Let me read reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely matches.

The Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt reference (1573604) shows a very similar pattern — plant collapsed sideways with mix of wilted/dried and still-green foliage on black plastic mulch. Strong match. One more view needed.

**Summary of evidence:**

- **Test image**: Whole plant completely collapsed/prostrate on black plastic mulch. Left portion shows dried/desiccated tissue; right portion still has greenish leaves. No fungal growth, sclerotia, or leaf spots visible. Rapid collapse pattern.

- **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt (1573604)**: Most visually similar — collapsed plant sideways with mix of wilted/brown dried tissue and still-green areas, on black plastic mulch. Strong match.

- **Bacterial_Wilt (5606056)**: Wilted but still standing on trellis — less collapsed than test.

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt (5593860)**: Heavily wilted but still standing — not fully collapsed like test.

- **Verticillium_Wilt (5606151)**: Lower leaf yellowing, plant still standing — doesn't match.

- **Southern_Blight, TSWV, CMV, Southern_Blight**: All clearly different patterns.

The test image best matches **Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato** — the complete sideways plant collapse with asymmetric desiccation of older tissue while newer foliage remains greenish is the clearest match among all reference images viewed.
